description: End-to-end bootstrap for a Kotlin Multiplatform (Android + iOS) app repository — collects `ui` (`compose` = Compose Multiplatform shared UI, `native` = Jetpack Compose on Android + SwiftUI on iOS over shared logic; asked via `AskUserQuestion` when absent), `branching` (`gitflow`/`main-only`), the app's identity (`app-name`, `application-id`, `bundle-id`, `namespace`, plus license and developer name/email/organization URL), and the shared pipeline parameters (integration branch `develop`, stable branch `main`, Java `17`, min SDK `26`, iOS deployment target, `open-source`, the repository `visibility` (detected via `gh repo view` or asked), `ci`, `ios-ci` (when the ~10×-cost macOS job runs: `all`/`stable`/`none`), `ci-tests` (`unit`, or `full` = also the iOS app's XCTest bundle on a simulator), `pages` (GitHub Pages vs. a workflow artifact for the Antora + Dokka docs), `distribution` (`none`/`internal`/`store` — Google Play/Firebase + TestFlight), `accessibility` (`enforce`/`report`/`off`/`none` — the UI tests' automated accessibility level, written by the scaffold to `.ui-quality.yml`), `sonar` plus its detail keys — each question stating the Actions-minutes / macOS-multiplier / SonarCloud / Pages cost facts for that visibility) once, prints a setup-mode statement (from scratch, or an inventory of the prior setup it found), then orchestrates `iru-setup-kmp-app` → `iru-setup-antora` → `iru-setup-kmp-gitignore` → `iru-setup-kmp-github-workflows` → `iru-setup-changelog` → `iru-setup-readme`, in that order, via `iru-isolated-skill-executor`, so nothing is asked twice — skipping the workflows step entirely (security block included) when `ci: no`. Invoke as `/iru-setup-kmp-repository`, optionally with `args` (`key: value` lines) to pre-resolve `ui`, `branching`, `mode` (`new`/`existing`), `open-source`, `visibility`, `ci`, `ios-ci`, `ci-tests`, `pages`, `accessibility`, `on-existing` (`ask`/`keep`/`update`/`replace`, forwarded only when supplied), `distribution`, `sonar` (+ `sonar-organization`/ `sonar-project-key`/`sonar-host-url`), `integration-branch`, `stable-branch`, `java-version`, `min-sdk`, `compile-sdk`, `ios-deployment-target`, `runner`, `xcode-version`, `team-id`, and every identity field, skipping the matching question. On an existing repository every component sub-skill warns about the prior setup it owns and asks Update / Keep as is / Replace per file (unless `on-existing` decides), and the final report states the action taken per component. Use whenever bootstrapping (or catching up) a Kotlin Multiplatform mobile app repository's full Gradle/Xcode/docs/gitignore/CI/changelog/README scaffold in one pass, instead of running six skills separately and re-answering the same questions each time.
